Construction of 3-Azabicyclo[3.1.0]hexane Backbone by the  
Reaction of Allenes with Allylamines via Tandem Michael  
Addition and Copper-Mediated Oxidative Carbanion Cyclization 
Hui Xu, Teng Han, Xiaoyan Luo,* and Wei-Ping Deng* 
Shanghai Key Laboratory of New Drug Design and School of Pharmacy, East China University of Science and Technology, 130 Meilo ng 
Road, Shanghai 200237, China 
 
Oxidative coupling | Allenes | Allylamine | 3-Azabicyclo[3,1,0]hexane | Miachel addition 
 
A facile synthetic method for the construction of 3-azabicyclo[3.1.0]hexane in the presence of copper catalyst system was developed. 
The reaction proceeds through Michael addition of allylamines with allenes followed by copper -mediated intramolecular oxidative 
carbanion 5 -exo-trig radical cyclization, affording potential biologically act ive 3 -azabicyclo[3.1.0]hexane derivatives in moderate to 
high yields (42%—85%).

Background and Originality Content 
3-Azabicyclo[3.1.0]hexane backbone is widely found as key 
structural unit in various natural products, pharmaceutically active 
molecules and drugs (Fi gure 1),[1] such as Bicifadine, a drug can -
didate for the treatment of low back pain in the Phase III clinical 
phase;[2] selective dopamine D3 receptor (DRD3) antagonist 
(GSK598809) for cocaine use disorder ;[3] Boceprevir for the treat -
ment of type I chronic hepatitis disease, ketone hexanone kinase 
(KHK) inhibitor for the treatment of non -alcoholic fatty liver 
dis-ease (NAFLD);[4] (+)-duocarmycin A, a kind of effective antibi -
otic with anti -tumor activity ;[5] Procymidone (procymidone), a 
new type of fungicide.[6] 
 
Figure 1  Bioactive molecules with 3-azabicyclo[3.1.0]hexane scaffold. 
Owing to their wide -ranging applications in organic synthesis 
and drug discovery, several syn thetic methods of 3 -azabicyclo-
[3.1.0]hexane have been reported .[7] Meanwhile, several exam-
ples of gold-catalyzed oxidative cyclopropanation have also been 
reported.[8] 
On the other hand, allene derivatives are a class of highly  im-
portant versatile building blocks in organic synthesis, which can be 
employed as special Michael acceptors for the reactions with 
different nucleophilic heteroatoms to construct corresponding 
heterocycles.[9-10] Meanwhile, we recently reported a series  of 
direct α,β -double electrophilic reaction s by the treatment of al -
lene-1,3-dicarboxylic esters with 1,3 -dicarbonyl derivatives or 
enamines under a mild I –/TBHP or H 2O2 reaction system to afford 
the multi -substituted furans, thiophens and pyrroles, respective-
ly.[11-12] Recently, Baskaran[13] et al . reported an efficient multi - 
component reaction for one-pot synthesis of cyclic amidine deriv -
atives with biologically important 3 -azabicyclo[3.1.0]alkane scaf -
fold by the reaction of ketenimine I and allylamines (Scheme 1a). 
Therefore, as part of our continuing efforts to develop synthetic 
methods for the formation of hete rocyles,[14] we envisaged that 
the use of allene as an alternative substrate instead of ketenimine 
I (Scheme 1a) would provide a new sy nthetic method for access -
ing 3-azabicyclo[3.1.0]hexane scaffold. Herein, we would like to 
describe a novel synthetic access to 3 -azabicyclo[3.1.0]hexane 
derivatives by the reaction of allylamines with allenes under  
1,8-diazabicyclo[5.4.0]undec-7-ene (DBU), affording carbanion A 
similar to carbanion II in Baskaran’s work, via tandem Michael 
addition and copper-mediated oxidative carbanion cyclization 
(Scheme 1b).

Having established the optimal reaction conditions, the sub -
strate scope of  this process was investigated ( Scheme 2). The 
reaction of allylamines 1a—1g with different substituent s at the 
N-position underwent smoothly, affording corresponding prod -
ucts 3aa—3ga in moderate to good yields (42 %—85%). Encour -
aged by these results, var ious substituents R 2 of allylamines 
1h—1i were then investigated, and it was found that allylamine 
with either alkyl or aryl grou p gave corresponding products 
3ha—3ra in good yields (62% —67%). Further extension of sub -
strate scope of allylamine with electron-withdrawing or elec -
tron-donating groups of aromatic substituents 1j—1r all reacted 
smoothly to furnish the products 3ja—3ra in good to high yields 
(53%—76%). F inally, allene 2b with ethyl ester was also found 
well tolerated, affording 3bb in 75% yield. In addition, the struc -
ture of 3ra was established by single crystal X -ray diffraction  
analysis (see Supporting Information).

3aa in 82% yield (Scheme 3a). On the other hand, an unexpected

Conclusions 
In summary, we have demonstrated a facile synthetic method 
for the construction of 3 -azabicyclo[3.1.0]hexane scaffold by the 
reaction of allylamine with electron -deficient allene through tan -
dem aza-Michael addition and intramolecular o xidative carbanion 
5-exo-trig radical cyclization and cyclopropanation in the presence 
of CuI. By using this novel synthetic method, a series of potential  
biologically active 3 -azabicyclo[3.1.0] hexane derivatives 3aa— 
3bb were obtained in moderate to high  yields (42 %—85%). A 
gram-scale synthesis of 3aa and its further tra nsformation under 
alkaline aqueous solution led to an unexpected carboxylic acid 
derivative 5 with an 3 -azabicyclo[3.1.0]hexane skeleton, which 
suggests potential application in a medicinal chemistry scenario. 
Experimental 
Allylamine 1 (0.2 mmol) and allene 2 (0.22 mmol) were added 
to THF (1.5 mL) at 50 ° C. The mixture was then stirred at the same 
temperature until the reaction was nearly completed monitored 
by the TLC. Afterwards, CuI (0.48 mmol) and DBU (0.56 mmol) 
were added to the mixture at 50 ° C. After the completion of the 
reaction indicated by TLC, the reaction mixture was concentrated 
under reduced pressure. The resulted residue was puriﬁed 
through ﬂash chromatography on silica gel (petroleum ether/ethyl 
acetate = 2/1) to aﬀord pure 3.

Hui Xu, Teng Han, Xiaoyan Luo,* and Wei-Ping Deng*

A facile synthetic method for the construction of 3-azabicyclo[3.1.0]hexane in the presence of copper catalyst system was developed. 
The reaction proceeds through Michael addition of allylamines with allenes followed by copper -mediated intramolecular oxidative 
carbanion 5 -exo-trig radical cyclization, affording potential biologically act ive 3 -azabicyclo[3.1.0]hexane derivatives in moderate to 
high yields (42%—85%).

Background and Originality Content 
3-Azabicyclo[3.1.0]hexane backbone is widely found as key 
structural unit in various natural products, pharmaceutically active 
molecules and drugs (Fi gure 1),[1] such as Bicifadine, a drug can -
didate for the treatment of low back pain in the Phase III clinical 
phase;[2] selective dopamine D3 receptor (DRD3) antagonist 
(GSK598809) for cocaine use disorder ;[3] Boceprevir for the treat -
ment of type I chronic hepatitis disease, ketone hexanone kinase 
(KHK) inhibitor for the treatment of non -alcoholic fatty liver 
dis-ease (NAFLD);[4] (+)-duocarmycin A, a kind of effective antibi -
otic with anti -tumor activity ;[5] Procymidone (procymidone), a 
new type of fungicide.[6] 
 
Figure 1  Bioactive molecules with 3-azabicyclo[3.1.0]hexane scaffold. 
Owing to their wide -ranging applications in organic synthesis 
and drug discovery, several syn thetic methods of 3 -azabicyclo-
[3.1.0]hexane have been reported .[7] Meanwhile, several exam-
ples of gold-catalyzed oxidative cyclopropanation have also been 
reported.[8] 
On the other hand, allene derivatives are a class of highly  im-
portant versatile building blocks in organic synthesis, which can be 
employed as special Michael acceptors for the reactions with 
different nucleophilic heteroatoms to construct corresponding 
heterocycles.[9-10] Meanwhile, we recently reported a series  of 
direct α,β -double electrophilic reaction s by the treatment of al -
lene-1,3-dicarboxylic esters with 1,3 -dicarbonyl derivatives or 
enamines under a mild I –/TBHP or H 2O2 reaction system to afford 
the multi -substituted furans, thiophens and pyrroles, respective-
ly.[11-12] Recently, Baskaran[13] et al . reported an efficient multi - 
component reaction for one-pot synthesis of cyclic amidine deriv -
atives with biologically important 3 -azabicyclo[3.1.0]alkane scaf -
fold by the reaction of ketenimine I and allylamines (Scheme 1a). 
Therefore, as part of our continuing efforts to develop synthetic 
methods for the formation of hete rocyles,[14] we envisaged that 
the use of allene as an alternative substrate instead of ketenimine 
I (Scheme 1a) would provide a new sy nthetic method for access -
ing 3-azabicyclo[3.1.0]hexane scaffold. Herein, we would like to 
describe a novel synthetic access to 3 -azabicyclo[3.1.0]hexane 
derivatives by the reaction of allylamines with allenes under  
1,8-diazabicyclo[5.4.0]undec-7-ene (DBU), affording carbanion A 
similar to carbanion II in Baskaran’s work, via tandem Michael 
addition and copper-mediated oxidative carbanion cyclization 
(Scheme 1b).

lected to verify the feasibility of this reaction (Table 1). The reac -
tion occurred in the presence of two equivalents of CuBr 2 to give 
the expected product 3aa, but it was accompanied with byprod -

Conclusions 
In summary, we have demonstrated a facile synthetic method 
for the construction of 3 -azabicyclo[3.1.0]hexane scaffold by the 
reaction of allylamine with electron -deficient allene through tan -
dem aza-Michael addition and intramolecular o xidative carbanion 
5-exo-trig radical cyclization and cyclopropanation in the presence 
of CuI. By using this novel synthetic method, a series of potential  
biologically active 3 -azabicyclo[3.1.0] hexane derivatives 3aa— 
3bb were obtained in moderate to high  yields (42 %—85%). A 
gram-scale synthesis of 3aa and its further tra nsformation under 
alkaline aqueous solution led to an unexpected carboxylic acid 
derivative 5 with an 3 -azabicyclo[3.1.0]hexane skeleton, which 
suggests potential application in a medicinal chemistry scenario. 
Experimental 
Allylamine 1 (0.2 mmol) and allene 2 (0.22 mmol) were added 
to THF (1.5 mL) at 50 ° C. The mixture was then stirred at the same 
temperature until the reaction was nearly completed monitored 
by the TLC. Afterwards, CuI (0.48 mmol) and DBU (0.56 mmol) 
were added to the mixture at 50 ° C. After the completion of the 
reaction indicated by TLC, the reaction mixture was concentrated 
under reduced pressure. The resulted residue was puriﬁed 
through ﬂash chromatography on silica gel (petroleum ether/ethyl 
acetate = 2/1) to aﬀord pure 3.
